source: Doom E3M4 House of Pain (Sandy Petersen)
title: House of Pain
brief: Inferno fortress whose footprint vaguely echoes organs (lungs/stomach). Dense combat, organic/flesh/marble contrast vs Phobos tech, overlapping rooms, and oppressive mood. Navigation relies on memorable grotesque shapes more than clean hubs.
pacing_notes: Higher skill ceiling: packs in irregular rooms, less 'safe teach', more relentless Inferno pressure with shape-based orientation.

part_designs.shape: narrow organic throat into wider body
part_designs.detail: Tone shift from techbase: shape and texture tell the story before any text.

part_designs.shape: paired side chambers left/right of a center axis
part_designs.elevation: mirrored-ish but not identical combat scripts
part_designs.detail: Bilateral layout is the landmark; player mentally maps 'left lung / right lung'.

part_designs.shape: irregular central cavity, not a rectangle
part_designs.elevation: pits and rises inside the gut
part_designs.detail: Hub by silhouette, not by clean tech lighting—still readable as 'the middle'.

part_designs.shape: dead-end pockets holding skull keys / switches
part_designs.triggers: skull doors elsewhere in the body
part_designs.detail: Gating still exists; presentation is hellish, not yellow-door-tech.

part_designs.shape: overlapping rooms, diagonal sightlines, odd angles
part_designs.detail: Complexity from shape + monster closet timing, not from longer corridors.

part_designs.shape: final chamber with clear but hostile end switch
part_designs.detail: Mood stays Inferno to the last frame; exit is a relief valve, not a bright lobby.

design_lessons: Theme via silhouette and texture, not only monsters
Irregular rooms for Inferno; orthogonality for tech
